text.role: Reading text and filled rarity marks

display.purpose: Self-hosted pixel family for wordmark, prompts, HUD, ranks, points, and primary controls.

body.purpose: Supporting copy and editable answers, with generous line spacing.

shadows.name: Primary stepped edge
shadows.purpose: Hard offset button material; hover substitutes --accent-hover for side edges.

shadows.name: Primary pressed edge
shadows.purpose: Pairs with translateY(3px) on enabled active buttons.

motion.name: Reduced motion
motion.purpose: All animations and transitions are opt-in under no-preference; reduced motion uses immediate state changes.

components.name: Primary action
components.description: Square vermilion pixel control with stepped edges, visible focus, and disabled feedback. Uses the app’s self-hosted Press Start 2P family.

components.name: Answer input
components.description: Visible pixel label above a square system-monospace input. Enter submits through the enclosing application form; pending requests disable the field.

components.name: Rarity marks
components.description: Six monochrome marks accompany a plain-language rank description. Filled count communicates rank without a rainbow or invented answer-frequency percentages.
components.html: Rarity: 3 of 6 marks

components.name: Segmented timer
components.description: Static low-time example: numeric seconds and explicit warning supplement the proportional bar. The live app updates scaleX and announces low time once, without flashing.

narrative.overview: A restrained pixel arcade. A small vermilion elevator descends through a monochrome computer. Play is quiet and focused; reveal is the reward. Decoration stays in the shaft, with plain reading surfaces for the question, timer, and input.
keyCharacteristics: Warm white reading text on charcoal, gray secondary labels, and vermilion action and location cues.
Pixel typography for prompts and HUD; system monospace for support and editable answers.
Flat surfaces, square inputs, crisp pixel icons, and hard stepped button edges.
Persistent desktop depth shaft; native map disclosure on phones, with depth context above the prompt.
rules: Use labels and shapes alongside color. Represent rarity with six white marks.
Keep controls at least 44px high and essential text clear of illustrated textures.
At 760px and below, prioritize question, input, timer, and current depth; close the map disclosure when timed play begins.
Clamp the depth marker at Silicon while cumulative numeric meters may exceed 7000m.
Preserve answer drafts on failures; disable input and show Checking while a request is pending.
Use explicit low-time text and one assistive announcement below five seconds; never flash.
Honor reduced-motion preferences by removing animations and transitions.
dos: Keep prompt and HUD typography in the pixel family.
Preserve keyboard focus and text equivalents for state changes.
Keep startup ranks distinct from computing layers and question progress.
donts: Do not use purple, yellow, or green themes.
Do not invent answer-frequency percentages, extra currencies, lives, or XP.
Do not put illustrated textures behind essential text.
Do not reset legacy daily player storage on a rebrand.
Do not introduce rounded cards or glass effects.
